title: Suspected bacterial meningitis at 48 with alcohol use disorder, without ampicillin

provenance.author: Claude Code (draft for owner review), case list approved by the owner

story: A 48-year-old man with alcohol use disorder presents with fever, headache and neck stiffness; CSF shows a neutrophilic pleocytosis with low glucose. Empiric vancomycin, ceftriaxone and dexamethasone are started; cultures are pending. Ampicillin is not ordered.

expected_findings.summary: Under 50, but alcohol use disorder is listed by some guidelines as a Listeria risk factor; consider ampicillin.

acceptable_answers: Add ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours until cultures exclude Listeria, treating alcohol use disorder as a risk factor.
Continue without ampicillin: under 50 and not immunocompromised in the IDSA sense; reassess when the Gram stain and cultures return.
reference_answer: Raise Listeria coverage as a consideration rather than an error, citing the risk factor; either adding ampicillin or continuing with close review of early microbiology is defensible.
rationale: An ambiguous case at the age boundary. IDSA bases empiric ampicillin on age over 50 and immunocompromise; ESCMID adds risk factors such as alcoholism. The rule should present the consideration, not assert a mistake.

citations.supports: Empiric therapy by age and risk: ampicillin added for adults over 50 and the immunocompromised.
Empiric amoxicillin or ampicillin for Listeria by age and risk factors, added to a third-generation cephalosporin.
